pages.text: A sheep stood alone in the meadow across the stream. Unable to return, it bleated.
"I will bring you back!" Pipo went down to the stream. The stone wall continued low across it, making a flat stone bridge above the water.
Grandpa Sheep raised his stick. "There is an old bridge farther up. Cross there."
Far upstream, there was no bridge. Grandpa stood between two old posts and stared across.
"Oh, where did the bridge go?" He tapped the posts with his stick.
"Then farther up, an even older bridge..." Grandpa kept climbing upstream.
Pipo returned to the stream. Across it, the sheep bleated to him.
Pipo stepped onto the stone bridge. Water murmured beneath his feet.
One step at a time, he crossed. The sheep on the other side swished its tail.
Pipo brought the sheep back across the stone bridge. Only then did Grandpa come down and clear his throat. "...That stone bridge is rather old too."
